title: Lesson 8 - Automatic Upgrades vs Manual Intervention Upgrade: Upgrade Strategy
description: Explain Managed Package Runtime vs. Standard Runtime, Automatic Upgrades, and Manual Intervention Upgrade.

questions.question: A customer has strict change control and several customizations that could break on a new OmniStudio version. Which upgrade approach is most appropriate?
options: Automatic upgrades, because they are easiest.
Manual intervention upgrades, so the org controls when and how a new version lands and can test first.
Upgrade only when the customer remembers to.
questions.explanation: An org with strict change control and fragile customizations should use manual intervention upgrades so it controls when and how a new version lands and can test in a sandbox first. Option A is wrong because automatic upgrades could land a breaking change without review. Option C is wrong because never upgrading blocks new features and fixes. Option D is wrong because upgrades should be planned, not remembered.

questions.question: An architect is choosing between automatic and manual upgrades for a low-risk org with no fragile customizations. What is the main benefit of automatic upgrades in this case?
options: They keep the org current with minimal effort.
They remove the need for a license.
questions.explanation: Automatic upgrades keep the org current with minimal effort, which is the right fit for a low-risk org that can accept the new version's behavior without review. Option B is wrong because a new version can still change behavior. Option C is wrong because licensing is separate from the upgrade path. Option D is wrong because no upgrade prevents all bugs.

questions.question: A team plans a manual intervention upgrade. What is the correct sequence before the production upgrade?
options: Upgrade production immediately and review afterward.
Review the release notes, test the new version in a sandbox against the org's artifacts, then schedule the production upgrade at a controlled time.
Skip testing because the new version is always safe.
Upgrade production and production only, with no sandbox.
questions.explanation: A manual intervention upgrade follows a controlled sequence: review the release notes, test the new version in a sandbox against the org's artifacts, then schedule the production upgrade at a controlled time. Option A is wrong because upgrading production before review risks breaking artifacts. Option C is wrong because new versions are not always safe. Option D is wrong because sandbox testing is a required step.
